teams.heading: Jake White reportedly turns to trusted Springbok ally; Fiji assistants still unnamed
teams.body: Jake White's assistant coaches remain unannounced. SA Rugby Magazine and Fiji Sun both report White turning to a trusted Springbok ally for his Fiji coaching team, but the reporting so far does not name that individual. White was appointed head coach as reported by Reuters on 13 October, ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Today's coverage returned no official confirmation of a complete backroom staff.

lead.why: No new men's national item cleared the bar, so the open Jake White backroom storyline leads, building on the appointment reported in shortlist item 5.

teams.heading: Manny Feyi-Waboso on track for Australia test despite hamstring tweak
teams.body: England's game-breaking wing Manny Feyi-Waboso is on track to face Australia in the Nations Championship despite tweaking a hamstring for Exeter against Newcastle. Scans have not revealed major damage, and Exeter's director of rugby Rob Baxter said: "He's had a scan and there's nothing I'm hearing from our physios saying there should be a long-term issue." Feyi-Waboso was due to miss Exeter's Champions Cup opener at Toulouse, but the Guardian reports he remains on course for England's Test against Australia. He has scored nine tries for England since his 2024 Six Nations debut.

lead.why: It is the freshest men's national-side item in the pack, an injury update on a key England wing ahead of the Australia Test.

teams.heading: French police open probe into Lions lock Hyron Andrews' death
teams.body: Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, was found unresponsive in a locked shower cubicle at the club's hotel on the Île de Ré, ahead of their Champions Cup match against La Rochelle, and French authorities have opened an investigation into his death. La Rochelle public prosecutor Arnaud Laraize confirmed to AFP that the case is being treated as a suspected accident, with an autopsy to follow and the gendarmerie handling it. Prosecutors said there were no signs of violence.

lead.why: It is the only new item on the shortlist, and a French investigation into a Champions Cup club player's death is the story most fans would be talking about.

teams.heading: Ciaran Frawley scores two as Connacht beat Saracens 45-36 in Champions Cup
teams.body: Ciaran Frawley scored two tries as Connacht beat Saracens 45-36 in the Champions Cup, with Andy Farrell watching from the stands. Planet Rugby says Frawley lost nothing in a shoot-out with an Ireland team-mate for Player of the Match, and that with Jack Crowley currently sidelined, his form arrives at a timely moment before the Nations Championship block. The site adds that it would be surprising not to see Frawley named in Ireland's 23 in November.

lead.why: A new item with a national-side angle, as Frawley's form is being read against Ireland's November selection, and it has not been reported on this tab.

teams.heading: Italy lose all three logged games, scoring 37 and conceding 131
teams.body: Italy have lost all three games in the table, scoring 37 points and conceding 131 for a difference of -94. Their most recent result was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round 3, the last of those three losses. Their next fixture is against South Africa, who beat Italy 32-14 at home in November 2025 in an International Friendly.

teams.heading: Scotland skipper Sione Tuipulotu sees brother make long-awaited Glasgow Warriors debut
teams.body: Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu has watched his brother finally make his Glasgow Warriors debut, a moment the Scotsman's report frames as a childhood dream fulfilled. The family story arrives as Scotland's men head for their next fixture, a Round 4 meeting with New Zealand, after a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round 3. Scotland sit fifth of 12 in the log after three matches: two wins and a defeat.

lead.why: It is the only new men's Scotland item in the pack; the other new items are women's coverage already published on this tab.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins says Wales players' influx into Prem can strengthen Welsh game
teams.body: Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins believes the influx of Wales players into the English Prem can benefit the Welsh game, telling BBC Sport that it is "opening up space for another young hooker, another young back-rower" in the United Rugby Championship. Jenkins, 23, has spent his whole senior career at Sandy Park and has started all three of Exeter's league matches this season. Wales captain Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake moved from the Ospreys to Gloucester over the summer.

lead.why: It is a men's Wales story with a named player and a direct quote, and it is not one of the items already run.

teams.heading: Loik Le Priol found guilty of killing former Pumas international Federico Aramburu
teams.body: A Paris court on 25 September found Loik Le Priol guilty of murdering former Argentina international Federico Aramburu and sentenced him to 26 years in prison. Aramburu, who won 22 caps for Argentina, was killed in March 2022 after an altercation at the Mabillon cafe, near Boulevard Saint-Germain. Romain Bouvier was found guilty of attempted murder and sentenced to 19 years. The pair are already serving sentences for a separate aggravated assault case, and had 10 days to appeal the ruling.

lead.why: The Edwards contract has already run today, and this is the strongest remaining item in the pack.

teams.heading: Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i misses five tackles as All Blacks exploit him in Sydney
teams.body: Planet Rugby's player ratings of Saturday's second Bledisloe Test have Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i looking lost in defence, with the centre missing five tackles in the 43-21 defeat at Accor Stadium. The former league man made an early offload that set up a Wallabies breakaway, but was often caught out of position and was exploited on multiple occasions by the All Blacks. Planet Rugby's verdict is that he was unable to smother the visitors' all-firing attack.

lead.why: It is the freshest men's national-side item in the pack that the Sunday edition has not already run, and it is about an individual Wallaby.

teams.heading: Japan score and concede 28 a game across last 11 matches
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308, averages of 28.1 and 28 a game. The biggest win in that window came at home against USA in September, a 63-14 victory in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Their most recent game was a 15-42 defeat to France in Round 3.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie to raise TMO penalty-try question at World Rugby's London meeting
teams.body: Dave Rennie believes the TMO will be a big topic when coaches and officials meet in London in a couple of weeks. The focus is Cam Roigard's cover tackle on Declan Meredith in Saturday's 43-21 win in Sydney, which denied the Wallabies a try. Rennie believes the officials correctly ruled that Roigard did not deliberately kick the ball, but asked what would happen if it had been a penalty try. "There are lots of questions to be asked around that."

lead.why: It is a new coach reaction on the men's national side, and it looks ahead to a World Rugby meeting rather than repeating the Sydney result.

teams.heading: Senatla leads Springboks-heavy Stormers to 49-12 Champions Cup win over Bristol
teams.body: In the Investec Champions Cup, the Stormers beat Bristol 49-12 with a Springboks-heavy side after a wasteful start. Man of the Match Seabelo Senatla scored the first try and laid on Leolin Zas' second, while Springboks props Ntuthuko Mchunu and Zachary Porthen were thrown on to batter the Bears' pack. JJ Kotze's first-half red card left the hosts a man down, but they still ran in the bonus-point win.

lead.why: The newest Springboks-linked item in the pack, and not the Bulls hat-trick already run today.
